recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-34306 unless a future cleanup effort explicitly decides to remove or normalize obsolete XPath spreadsheet cells that are no longer part of the current model.
issue_request: FHIR-34306 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction for R5, raised against R4/R4B, asking that ELD-12 on ElementDefinition.binding.valueSet stop unintentionally prohibiting contained ValueSet resources by allowing value set references beginning with '#'.
initial_application: The Jira record shows FHIR-I approved the technical correction by a 15-0-1 motion on 2021-11-22, later comments cite PR #1608, the R5 commit ba999eaa83, and the R4B PR #1733. Git history also shows 94d2f40b28 and 6e414afc16 applying the same issue to source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml before ba999eaa83 adjusted the XPath-era column.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is still an active normative datatype in source/fhir.ini, and the active spreadsheet source now says ELD-12 allows http:, https:, urn:, or # in both the human text and the FHIRPath expression. The only stale-looking current cell is the old XPath column, but ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath is disabled in the spreadsheet and source/fhir.ini maps it as removed due to lack of use and maintenance; R5 history generated from the applied source includes the corrected human/FHIRPath surface and no ELD-12 XPath entry. Confluence minutes confirm the FHIR-I approval, and the only Zulip hit found was an agenda note with no conflicting rationale.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current built ElementDefinition constraint already permits contained ValueSet references. No source files were changed.
